identity.title: Hydronephrosis (bilateral or solitary kidney) on renal POCUS

technique.how: Curvilinear probe in the posterior axillary line (right ~liver window, left more posterior/cephalad), long and short axis of each kidney; fan through the whole kidney. Hydronephrosis is anechoic dilatation of the renal pelvis/calyces: mild (pelvis only), moderate (calyceal ballooning), severe (cortical thinning). Always scan both kidneys and the bladder.
technique.prerequisites: Operator trained in renal POCUS; scan the bladder first (a full bladder or retention can cause bilateral mild hydronephrosis).

interpretation.positive_finding: Any hydronephrosis in flank pain raises the probability of a ureteric stone (pooled LR+ 2.85), and moderate-or-greater hydronephrosis is highly specific (0.94); bilateral hydronephrosis or hydronephrosis of a solitary kidney in AKI indicates obstructive uropathy needing decompression.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absent hydronephrosis lowers but does not exclude obstruction (LR- 0.39 for stones; sens 0.85-0.90 in AKI cohorts), especially early, with dehydration, or with retroperitoneal fibrosis/malignant encasement.
interpretation.pitfalls: Parapelvic cysts, prominent renal vasculature, extrarenal pelvis, pregnancy and a full bladder mimic hydronephrosis; volume depletion and early obstruction hide it. Unilateral hydronephrosis does not explain AKI unless the other kidney is absent or non-functioning.
interpretation.changes_what: Bilateral/solitary-kidney hydronephrosis in AKI: decompress and refer to urology; unilateral with flank pain: manage as ureteric stone, CT if septic; absent: pursue non-obstructive causes.

estimates.population: Adult ED patients with renal colic symptoms; 5 high-quality studies, n=1773
estimates.reference_standard: CT evidence of stone or hydronephrosis, direct stone visualisation, or surgical findings
estimates.quote: 70.2% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 67.1%-73.2%) and 75.4% (95% CI = 72.5%-78.2%), respectively. The calculated positive and negative likelihood ratios were 2.85 and 0.39.

estimates.target_condition: Nephrolithiasis (moderate or greater hydronephrosis on POCUS)
estimates.population: Adult ED patients with renal colic symptoms; two of the meta-analysis studies
estimates.reference_standard: CT evidence of stone or hydronephrosis
estimates.quote: the finding of moderate or greater hydronephrosis yielded a specificity of 94.4% (95% CI = 92.7%-95.8%)

estimates.population: Hospitalised adults with AKI, single Canadian centre; 65 patients with PoCUS and reference imaging, 124 kidneys
estimates.quote: PoCUS had a sensitivity of 85% (95% CI 71-94%) and specificity of 78% (95% CI 68-87%) for the detection of hydronephrosis.

estimates.target_condition: Renal tract obstruction in acute kidney injury
estimates.population: Adults admitted with AKI to an acute internal medicine unit, UK; protocolised POCUS vs departmental ultrasound (quality improvement project)
estimates.quote: POCUS can rapidly and reliably diagnose renal tract obstruction, showing a sensitivity of 90% and a specificity of 100%.

sources.citation: Wong C, Teitge B, Ross M, Young P, Robertson HL, Lang E. The Accuracy and Prognostic Value of Point-of-care Ultrasound for Nephrolithiasis in the Emergency Department: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. Acad Emerg Med. 2018;25(6):684-698.
Gaudreau-Simard M, Saiyin T, McInnes MDF, et al. Test characteristics of point-of-care ultrasonography in patients with acute kidney injury. Ultrasound J. 2024;16(1):11.
Nepal S, Dachsel M, Smallwood N. Point-of-care ultrasound rapidly and reliably diagnoses renal tract obstruction in patients admitted with acute kidney injury. Clin Med (Lond). 2020;20(6):541-544.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use a negative scan to exclude obstruction in volume-depleted patients, early obstruction, or suspected malignant/retroperitoneal encasement; obtain formal imaging.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Obstructed kidney with fever or sepsis (infected obstructed system) needs emergent decompression (nephrostomy/stent) and urology; bilateral obstruction with hyperkalaemia needs immediate relief.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Grading of mild hydronephrosis is the least reproducible element; the meta-analysis found no threshold effect but studies used variable operator experience.
safety_scope.skill_assumption: Emergency or internal-medicine physician with basic renal POCUS training (a short course plus supervised scans); AKI cohorts used protocolised scans by trained generalists, not sonographers.

extraction_notes: Wong 2018 pooled estimates are for stone disease in renal colic (any hydronephrosis = positive), not for obstruction in AKI; LRs are those calculated by the authors. Two AKI cohorts added as separate estimates: Gaudreau-Simard 2024 (small, 65 patients, mixed reference) and Nepal 2020 (QI project, radiology US as reference, CIs not in abstract). Publication years taken from PubMed records (Wong e-pub 2018, journal issue 2018; Nepal issue Nov 2020, PubMed year 2021).
